glosses: Partager ; distribuer ; attribuer à chacun sa part.

examples.text: L'ustensile employé est une cocotte en fonte très épaisse, assez grande. La fonte est longue à chauffer mais, à travers sa matière, la chaleur se répartit plus régulièrement.

Démouler dans une petite assiette afin que le sirop de datte se répartisse sur le flan.
Répartir les biens d’une succession entre plusieurs cohéritiers. — Répartir des bénéfices, les contributions.
La ville était trop petite pour loger toutes les troupes, il fallut en répartir la moitié dans les villages voisins.

examples.text: Er verteilte den Dünger gleichmäßig über die gesamte Rasenfläche.

examples.text: Die Polizei verteilte sich über den gesamten Campus.

glosses: etwas in seine Komponenten aufteilen, in seine Einzelteile auflösen

examples.text: Die neue Fräsmaschine wurde in ihre Einzelteile zerlegt.

Mein Psychiater zerlegt in jeder Sitzung meine letzten Träume.

glosses: To divide into portions and dispense.

examples.text: He distributed the bread amongst his followers.

A network of children distributes flyers to every house.

Above all, the 48-page timetables of the new service, which have been distributed free at every station in the scheme, are a model to the rest of B.R. glosses: To classify or separate into categories.

examples.text: The database distributed verbs into transitive and intransitive segments.

glosses: To separate (type which has been used) and return it to the proper boxes in the cases.
To spread (ink) evenly, as upon a roller or a table.
To employ (a term) in its whole extent; to take as universal in one premise.

examples.text: A term is said to be distributed when it is taken universal, so as to stand for everything it is capable of being applied to.

glosses: To have employees working remotely from multiple locations.

examples.text: distributed business; distributed employee

glosses: To set aside for a purpose.

examples.text: Please do not eat the meringue, as it is allocated for the dinner party tomorrow.

glosses: To distribute according to a plan, generally followed by the adposition to.

examples.text: The bulk of K–12 education funds are allocated to school districts that in turn pay for the cost of operating schools.

glosses: To reserve a portion of memory for use by a computer program.

examples.text: The memory manager allocates memory to requesting processes until there is no more memory available or until there are no more processes waiting for memory.

glosses: A writ authorizing payment, allowance, grant.
To divide and distribute portions of a whole.

examples.text: The controlling party had apportioned the voting districts such that their party would be favored in the next election.

glosses: Specifically, to do so in a fair and equitable manner; to allocate proportionally.

examples.text: The children were required to dump all of their Halloween candy on the table so that their parents could apportion it among them.
